newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia stocks end firm, seen biding time.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia stocks end firm, seen biding time.

text.p: Slovenian shares reversed a losing streak to end firmer on Thursday.
But traders lamented over low turnover which they expect to continue until the political situation becomes clearer.
"Turnover is low because of the political situation -- foreign investors will probably wait until the new government is formed," Karmen Cerar, a trader of brokerage Poteza said.
Analysts said forming the new government may take several weeks as the country's second general election on November 10 brought an undecided result.

The current ruling Liberal Democrats emerged as the strongest single party with 25 out of 90 parliamentary seats, but are facing a rightist "Spring" alliance comprising three parties which together received 45 seats, missing only one seat for an absolute majority.
The 10-share SBI index rose 0.42 percent or 4.82 points to 1,149.9. Overall 12 shares rose, four fell and one remained unchanged, while another eight were untraded.
Turnover fell to 166.7 million tolars from 247.8 million.
Port Luka Koper, completing its second day of trading, was the most actively traded share, firming 2.64 percent to 2,258 tolars on volume of 65.1 million tolars.
Market participants said Luka's price and volume in the future will largely depend upon whether the state, which owns 51 percent of the company's equity, would approve purchases by foreign investors.
Brokerage Dadas was the biggest gainer, surging 10.65 percent to 10,910 tolars on volume of 39 shares for total turnover of 405,190 tolars.
Ordinary shares of bank Hipotekarna banka Brezice led the day's decliners, falling 7.27 percent or 290 tolars to 3,700 tolars on volume of 40 shares.
